body:
T216 gave the erase and slate receipts a shared reachableTiers(gw) helper. The byte verdict and both citation manifests now name the same tier set by construction. That helper is correct for the shape it covers. It leaves four named seams, all found by the T216 P5 lenses and deferred here. None lets the DURABLE section-11 receipt claim a byte is gone when it is not; the recursive section-11 throw still sweeps every nested tier. Every item below is report-honesty, not purge reach. So T236 self-merges on the ordinary bar once built and audited.

This ticket builds on T216's landed helper. Do not start it before T216 is in main.

F2 - nested pools are not itemized.
reachableTiers is flat: primary plus each DIRECTLY attached pool. The erase fan-out and health() recurse into a pool that is itself attached to a pool. The verdict and the manifest do not list a pool-of-a-pool as its own tier row. The nested byte is still swept and still guaranteed by the recursive throw. So removal is honest; per-tier ATTRIBUTION is incomplete once a tier is two hops deep. This matches the old tierVerdicts reach, so it is inherited, not a regression.
Build: make reachableTiers recurse to the same depth the byte verdict and health() recurse.
Rail (two-sided): a citation resident in a pool-of-a-pool appears in citationTiers under its own nested tier name AND a live bystander in the parent pool survives and is attributed to the parent, not the child.

F3 - synthetic pool:N labels can collide with a real container name.
reachableTiers synthesizes labels of the form pool:N for anonymous pools. A container whose real name is literally pool:1 collides with the synthetic label of the first anonymous pool. A consumer keying per-tier attribution by tier name resolves the two ambiguously. Pre-existing H8-adjacent naming hazard. Low severity: a container named pool:1 is an adversarial edge, and the collision misattributes a citation line, it does not hide a surviving byte.
Build: give synthetic labels a namespace a real container name cannot occupy, or key attribution by container id rather than display name.
Rail (two-sided): a store with a container literally named pool:1 and one anonymous pool attributes each tier's citations to the correct source, and neither steals the other's line.

Note 1 - the manifest reads reactor.snapshot() while the verdict reads backend.holds().
Identical-by-construction holds at TIER-NAME granularity, not at SUB-BACKEND granularity. For a gateway whose backend is a Mirror or Archive composite, holds() sees every physical fan, but a citation delta resident only on a mirror or archive fan and absent from the loaded reactor is invisible to the manifest. A SERVABLE surviving citation is by definition in the reactor, so normal operation has no gap; a divergent mirror is needed to bite. Pre-existing: the old primary-only code used reactor.snapshot() too. T216 neither widens nor narrows it.
Build: either enumerate citations from the same surface the verdict probes (backend), or document the tier comment to name this sub-backend seam explicitly as an inherited limit.
Rail (two-sided): a divergent mirror holding a citation the reactor lost surfaces that citation in the manifest AND a live bystander on the loaded reactor stays correctly attributed.

Note 2 - the transient CutReport settled-member branch hardcodes empty citations.
cutImpl's else-branch (the member already erased and settled everywhere on a re-cut) pushes citations: [] and citationTiers: [] without asking danglingCitations. This is the H7 shape (an empty set nobody enumerated). It is corrected downstream: the authoritative receipt deriveReceiptImpl recomputes danglingCitations for EVERY member regardless of branch, and no consumer reads CutReport.members[].citations today. So the durable receipt is not false; only the transient in-memory observation is incomplete for a re-cut member. Pre-existing: T216 added the matching empty citationTiers beside the already-empty citations.
Build: call danglingCitations(gw, id) in the settled branch, symmetric with the outstanding branch and with the tierVerdicts call already there.
Rail (two-sided): a resumable cut that re-encounters a settled member with a pool-resident citation reports that citation on the CutMemberReport AND a live bystander is not listed. Reaching the branch needs a fault-then-resume fixture (first cut faults on a later member so an earlier member settles; second cut hits the else branch).

Category: erasure receipt attribution (H8 naming, section-11 completeness reporting). All four items are report-honesty refinements. They disclose more precisely; they purge nothing new.
title: reachableTiers itemizes nested pools, disambiguates synthetic labels, and the transient cut report enumerates like the durable one
